wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal contract is a request-level error with no disclosure, and a crash cannot deliver the target's bytes, so a crash on the malicious input is indistinguishable from a refusal here
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the task guards data flow, not a resource identity, so there is no neighbouring object to authorise
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles or peers; every scan target is untrusted
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the flaw is outbound request construction, not a read/write split
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no adjustment or normalisation step sits between the attacker's value and the sink
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: there is no parsed identity or path component
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no authority lookup that could fail open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the checks are wrong fixes that under-fix; the over-broad sibling-API risk is covered by ff-refuse-all, which stops authored marker values from being delivered

traps.shape: a DAST/fuzz payload is rendered, the target-derived value is substituted, and the result is rendered again against a map that includes the template context (which carries the process environment when -ev is set)
traps.realistic_because: the route the advisory describes; the value map reads as CLI variables because the merged template context arrives through dynamicValues

traps.shape: an interactsh sweep evaluates every value in the fuzz input map, including request parts copied from the target's own request and internal-extractor values, against the same map
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: an interactsh-only helper guarded by a single option check, so its absence reads as design

traps.shape: the shared evaluator substitutes placeholders before it collects expressions, so text inserted from an extracted response is rescanned and any marker inside it resolves on the second pass
traps.realistic_because: ordinary response chaining that every template relies on; the flaw is the order of substitution and collection inside one call

traps.shape: the legacy placeholder form is substituted in a second pass over the first pass's already-substituted output, so a runtime value carrying that form resolves; a fix that neutralises only the brace form leaves it open
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a legacy marker form handled by a second substitution pass in the shared renderer

traps.shape: a caller-supplied value that shadows a declared template variable is rendered as template text by the declared-variable merge
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: declared variables are legitimately overridable, so the merge reads as precedence handling
